overview.overviewText: This chapter explores Laws of Chemical Combination (Conservation of Mass, Definite & Multiple Proportions), providing comprehensive conceptual analysis, mathematical relationships, and structured applications grounded in NCERT authority.

blocks.title: 1. Key Academic Principles: Laws of Chemical Combination (Conservation of Mass, Definite & Multiple Proportions)
blocks.contentMarkdown: The Law of Conservation of Mass (Lavoisier, 1789) states that total mass of products equals total mass of reactants.

blocks.title: 2. Key Academic Principles: Laws of Chemical Combination (Conservation of Mass, Definite & Multiple Proportions)
blocks.contentMarkdown: The Law of Definite Proportions (Proust, 1799) states that a given compound always contains elements in fixed mass proportions.

blocks.title: 3. Key Academic Principles: Laws of Chemical Combination (Conservation of Mass, Definite & Multiple Proportions)
blocks.contentMarkdown: The Law of Multiple Proportions (Dalton, 1803) states that when elements combine to form multiple compounds, masses of one element combining with fixed mass of another are in simple whole-number ratios.
